[issue by FlashHUN]

	at java.base/java.lang.module.Configuration.<init>(Configuration.java:139)
	at java.base/java.lang.module.Configuration.resolveAndBind(Configuration.java:493)
	at MC-BOOTSTRAP/cpw.mods.modlauncher@11.0.4/cpw.mods.modlauncher.ModuleLayerHandler.buildLayer(ModuleLayerHandler.java:75)
	at MC-BOOTSTRAP/cpw.mods.modlauncher@11.0.4/cpw.mods.modlauncher.ModuleLayerHandler.buildLayer(ModuleLayerHandler.java:87)

On a previous version (MC 1.20.6, Architectury API 12.1.2, NeoForge 20.6.77-beta, KFF 5.1.0) the project ran perfectly fine, can't figure out whether the issue is with KFF or Architectury so making [an issue for Architectury too](https://github.com/architectury/architectury-api/issues/543).

Architectury Enabled Platforms: Fabric, NeoForge
Minecraft Version: 1.21
Architectury API Version: 13.0.4
NeoForge Version: 21.0.86-beta
KotlinForForge Version: 5.4.0

[comment by thedarkcolour (owner)]
This is a bug in Loom. It doesn't happen in plain ModDevGradle/NeoGradle.
That being said, have you tried excluding KFF's transitive dependency on FancyModLoader? Has group: `net.neoforged.fancymodloader` and name: `loader`.

[comment by FlashHUN (none)]
Excluding it solved the issue, thank you!

[comment by double-pi (none)]
@FlashHUN how did u fix it? What does it mean "excluding KFF's transitive dependency"?

[comment by c-Caelum (none)]
I assume you've either solved it or given up at this point, but in build files, we have something called transitive dependencies. These basically mean that a project you depend on (for example `example-mod`) needs something, and so it passes it onto your project. `exclude` lets you manually get rid of one of these transitive dependencies, like so:
```gradle
implementation("my-example-mod-dependency:1.0") {
    exclude group: "my.example.exclusion.group", module "moduleToExclude"
}
```
